В каталоге /home/az/Projects/yeah-selfdev-1 лежит репозиторий Yeah — агента на Emacs Lisp, который работает внутри Emacs. Нужно выполнить волну 41 плана (docs/PLAN.md §18.1): сделать детерминированной проверку моста.

Дефект: одна проверка моста — гонка. Проверка tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el читает буфер подключённого Emacs сто двадцать раз, пока отдельный поток крутится и делает родителя медленным, и падает только когда ответ действительно потерян. 16 ноября 2026 шесть прогонов доказательства дали пять укусов и один промах: control дошёл до предмета, проверка после control всё равно прошла, claim вышел inconclusive, а карта метода вышла unknown. Код виноват не был — виновато было доказательство.

Что должно измениться: проверка перестаёт гнаться за предметом и начинает им распоряжаться. Потеря ответа становится условием, которое проверка сама создаёт — барьер, который ждёт родитель, или хук, который принадлежит проверке, — так что один и тот же вход даёт один и тот же вердикт каждый раз. Control проверяемого claim'а — та же схема с одним шагом, убранным, и тогда проверка обязана падать на своём же утверждении, а не на краше Emacs и не на таймауте.

Что нужно сделать:
1. Пере-регистрировать claim bridge-keeps-the-answer в spec.json с control'ом, который кусается каждый раз (register: fact, требование: проверка моста).
2. Добавить новый claim the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction: проверка моста даёт один и тот же вердикт на десяти последовательных прогонах control'а, и control кусается на каждом из них.
3. Критерии выхода: десять последовательных прогонов control'а кусаются, каждый падает на утверждении проверки; и проверка, запущенная без control'а, проходит стабильно.

Работай в этом каталоге. Сначала прочитай AGENTS.md, docs/PLAN.md (разделы 18.1 и 17), docs/ENGINEERING.md, ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md (раздел 11 — журнал ловушек), затем lib/yeah-bridge.el и саму проверку. Правила репозитория обязательны: lib/ — только Elisp, одна фича на файл, публичные символы с yeah-, внутренние с yeah--, доменные ошибки — user-error или структурированные ошибки, никакой телеметрии, никаких глобальных дефолтов и глобальных перехватов gptel, подпроцессы через make-process. Проверяй свою работу теми же командами, которыми проверяет репозиторий: ./scripts/dev byte-compile-all, ./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el, ./scripts/dev check tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el. Проверка моста поднимает настоящий Emacs-демон: emacs и emacsclient лежат в ~/.nix-profile/bin, а в переменной EMACS укажи этот путь, если проверка его не найдёт сама.

Когда работа сделана и проверена, закончи через инструмент finish и вкратце скажи, что изменилось и чем ты это проверил.

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

## Current warnings for every agent

- This is a kernel prototype, not a usable coding product.
- The parity with other harnesses was piloted on 2026-11-15, and the
  difference the pilot found was a defect of the turn, not a difference of
  quality: after the results of the tool calls arrive, the model may answer
  with an empty message, and the turn took that as the end of the work and
  stopped without the effect (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot of the
  parity").  The defect is fixed (the claim
  `an-empty-answer-does-not-end-the-run'), and the pilot on the fixed turn
  moved one task of three; the nudge now carries the state of the work
  (the claim `a-silence-nudge-carries-the-state-of-the-work'), because the
  provider goes silent after every batch of tool results and the model was
  answering the nudge by starting the work over.  With that, Yeah passes
  two tasks of three and pi passes three.  The third task failed in the
  tools: the `read` of a file nobody has edited yet returns no tick, and
  the `edit` refused the tick the model guessed as stale although the file
  has not changed; wave 26 makes a guessed tick ignored rather than
  refused (the claim
  `a-guessed-tick-does-not-refuse-an-unchanged-file'), and that task of the
  pilot passes now.  The provider was overloaded for hours (HTTP 529 to both
  harnesses), so the pilot of 15:02 measured one task of three and two
  blocked runs: the runner records a run the provider stopped as **blocked**,
  neither a pass nor a failure (the claim
  `a-provider-failure-is-not-a-failure-of-the-agent').  The pilot of 15:39, on
  the code of wave 28, measured two tasks of three — Yeah passed both of them
  and pi passed all three — and the third was blocked, because the transport
  to the provider died.  The parity of that run is not measured either.  The
  pilot of 17:06, on the code of waves 30+31, measured one task of three for
  Yeah and two of three for pi: all three runs of Yeah ended `unfinished`,
  because the provider goes silent, and the one task that failed in the tools
  failed on the **version token** of the file — the model copied 58 of the 64
  characters of the digest and the edit refused the edit of a file that had
  not changed (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot that measured the copy of the
  version token").  The pilot of 17:23, on the code of wave 32, measured two
  tasks of three for Yeah and three of three for pi: the token of the file is
  short now, the read handed out twelve characters, and the tasks the model
  worked on passed.  The task that Yeah failed failed on the provider: the
  model announced the fix ("Fixing it to use floating-point division:") and
  called no tool (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot after the token became
  short").  The pilot of 2026-11-16 06:43–06:48, on the code of wave 33, measured
  two tasks of three for Yeah and three of three for pi, and the pilot of
  07:04, on the code of wave 34, measured one task of three for Yeah and three
  of three for pi.  Both failures were the same failure of the model and not of
  the harness: the model read the files of the task and never called the tool
  that would change them, while the guards of waves 29, 32, 33 and 34 were
  never in the way (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the pilot after
  wave 34").  The pilot of 08:07, on the code of wave 35, measured two tasks of
  three for Yeah and three of three for pi, and the third task of Yeah was
  blocked: the transport to the provider died with "Curl failed with exit code
  28" after the model had read the file and computed the sum.  A run that the
  provider stops is blocked and not a failure of the agent, and it says
  nothing about either harness (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the
  pilot after wave 35").  The pilot of 10:00, on the code of wave 36, measured
  two tasks of three for Yeah and three of three for pi, and the third task of
  Yeah failed in the tools: the model read the file, computed the sum with
  `bash` (the tool answered 100) and then answered with an empty message three
  times; the harness nudged three times, every nudge carrying the state of the
  work, and the run ended "unfinished" with the nudge budget spent.  The file
  was never written, so the runner recorded a failure of the agent; that is
  the shape the provider has had for two days, and `write-new-file` passed in
  the same pilot, so the write path of the code of wave 36 works (docs/
  LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the pilot after wave 36").  The
  pilot of 10:44, on the code of wave 37, measured the same: two tasks of
  three for Yeah and three of three for pi, and the third task of Yeah
  failed in the tools the same way — the model read the file, ran `bash`,
  and then answered with an empty message; the harness nudged it with the
  state of the work, and the model went silent again (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md,
  "The live checks and the pilot after wave 37").  The pilot of 13:12, on the
  code of wave 38, measured one task of three for Yeah and three of three for
  pi: two tasks of Yeah failed in the same shape — the model read the files,
  and then answered with an empty message three times, and the run ended
  "unfinished" with the nudge budget spent.  The row of such a run names the
  shape of it since wave 38, so the reader of the pilot sees the cause of the
  failed check and not only its verdict; the verdict of the row is still the
  verdict, because the classification of a run that did not finish is a
  decision of the owner (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the
  pilot after wave 38").  The threshold of the
  parity is a decision of the owner (docs/PLAN.md §13), and nobody may quote
  the pilot as a verdict about parity.
- A decision that arrives while the tools of the previous decision are still
  running no longer breaks the run: the turn keeps the calls, runs them when
  the running batch has settled, and gives the model the results of every
  batch together (wave 28, the claims
  `a-decision-that-arrives-while-the-tools-run-does-not-break-the-run' and
  `the-same-tool-call-does-not-run-twice').  The live checks of 15:38 hold
  no transition error at all.  The live coding task still fails, and it fails
  for another reason: the model of the provider answers with an empty message
  and the run ends with the record "unfinished" — the work is not done, and
  the run says so.
- The read of a file shows the file on disk, but the tick it hands out
  belongs to the buffer that visits the file: when Emacs holds unsaved
  changes of that file, the model sees the disk and the edit applies to the
  buffer.  Wave 29 refused that case when the model presents the version of
  the read; wave 33 makes the refusal the answer of every edit, with a
  version or without one, because a read of the disk cannot show the changes
  of the person (the claim
  `an-edit-never-lands-on-a-file-with-unsaved-changes').  The write takes the
  same short version token and is refused when the file changed after the
  read that handed it out (the claim
  `a-write-never-lands-on-a-file-that-changed'); the token of the write is
  optional, so a model that presents no version writes without that guard.
  A write of a file that Emacs holds unsaved changes of is not refused: the
  write goes to the disk and the buffer becomes stale — that is open in
  docs/PLAN-NEXT.md.
- The harness opens the files of the project on behalf of the model, and
  Emacs runs the local variables of a file and the directory-local variables
  of its directory when it opens one.  That code is the code of the project,
  and the project is untrusted input: a `mode:` entry names a function that
  Emacs calls, and an `eval:` entry is Elisp that Emacs evaluates.  The edit
  opens the file through `yeah-untrusted-open-file` (lib/yeah-untrusted.el),
  where that machinery is neutralized whatever the configuration of the
  Emacs is (wave 34, the claim
  `an-edit-never-runs-the-local-variables-of-the-project').  The price is
  named: the mode line of the file is part of its content, so it is ignored,
  and the buffer of the person shows the file in the mode of its name.
- Every read now hands the model the version of the file as well: the digest
  of its bytes (lib/yeah-version.el). The edit checks that version and is
  refused when the file changed after the read, so an edit never lands on a
  file the model did not read; it is also refused when Emacs holds unsaved
  changes of the file, because a read of the disk cannot show them. A
  version that no read handed out is ignored, like a tick that no read handed
  out. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §D5 was amended, not weakened: it names the
  version as the second form of the state a read returns.
- The process of the ACP server outlives the agent when the client keeps its
  pipe open, and some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of
  userspace. The read loop of the server is not the cause (an idle server
  costs no CPU and leaves on EOF) and the wait for a turn is not either (about
  four per cent of a core): the spin is on the path of the live request of the
  provider, and the loop is not localized yet. Nobody may quote the ACP
  server as free of this until a canary says so — docs/PLAN.md §17.1.
- The version token is short (12 characters of the digest) and a refusal of a
  token that does not match names the token, not the file, and reports the
  current token so that the retry lands: the pilot of 17:06 measured a model
  that copied 58 of the 64 characters of the digest and an edit that refused
  a file that had not changed (wave 32, the claims
  `a-version-token-is-short-enough-to-copy' and
  `an-edit-refuses-a-wrong-token-with-the-current-one'). A model can still
  lose a character of twelve, and the harness cannot make the model retry.
- A decision that repeats a call that is already running is dropped, and the
  drop is now in the journal: the event `tool-dropped` carries the tool, the
  reason and the arguments, so a reader of the log tells a repeated decision
  from a decision that never came (wave 30). The model is not told that its
  repetition was refused, because a tool that runs twice would repeat its
  side effect; the identity of a call is still the tool and its arguments.
  docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §D1 was amended, not weakened: the vocabulary it
  names now includes dropped calls.
- The checks read the journals through one reader
  (`tests/support/yeah-journal-files.el`), and that reader skips the lock
  files of Emacs (`.#`) next to a journal and survives a journal that
  vanishes between the scan and the read. A check that crashes on the
  filesystem does not fail on its assertion, and the method reads a crashed
  verifier as an error and not as a proven control (wave 31).
- Stage 7 is implemented offline: an agent preset is a file (a Markdown or
  Org header and a body), and a child runs for real in its own session with
  only the tools it was granted. The fixed-point demonstration passes with
  a live model: a child repairs a Yeah canary and the canary passes
  afterwards (tests/live/live-fixed-point.el, one child). Parallel
  children and the cheaper child model are not implemented yet; an Org
  preset header and the Org export of a session are (lib/yeah-agent.el,
  lib/yeah-org.el).
- The delegation of a child is a tool of the kernel (wave 35): `delegate`
  names an agent preset and a task, and the child runs in a session of its
  own, on the model of the preset, with the tools of the preset and with
  the instructions of the preset; every tool outside the preset is refused
  to it. The turn of the parent is not held: `delegate` answers at once
  with the id of the child, the child answers on its own, and
  `delegate-result` reports what became of it. A delegation changes the
  world, so the Plan profile denies it (lib/yeah-delegate.el,
  docs/PLAN.md §16.18).
- A delegation belongs to the run that asked for it (wave 36). The audit of
  wave 35 found the defect: the tool that delegates remembered the sessions of
  the runs whose calls were allowed and took the first of them, so a
  delegation could be written into the journal of another run, and a call that
  failed left its session behind for the next delegation to take. The run binds
  the session it writes into while it dispatches the call (lib/yeah-session.el,
  lib/yeah-turn.el), and the child of that call is written into the journal of
  that run; a call with no run has no journal and is refused. The id of a child
  is short (`sub-1`), because the model has to copy it back and a long token is
  copied with an error; a wrong id is refused by name, and the refusal names
  the children that do exist. A child has a time of its own (`timeout:` in the
  preset, 900 seconds by default): a child that ran out of time is cancelled,
  and the parent is told why. Several children in one turn of the parent work
  already — the audit proved it, and the plan that said otherwise was wrong.
  Not implemented then: the depth of the tree of the children and the children
  themselves were kept in the running Emacs and not in the journal; wave 37
  moved the tree into the journal (docs/PLAN.md §16.19, §16.20, §17.1).
- Wave 37 moved the tree of the children into the journal: the journal of the
  run holds the short id, the session and the depth of every child, and the
  journal of the child holds where that child stands in the tree (its parent,
  its depth and the id the model calls it by). A harness that starts again
  reads the tree from there: the child of a run is found by the id the model
  was given, what became of it is told, and a child the journal holds no end
  of is not reported as a child that still works — the restart ends the child
  as well, because the child runs in the same Emacs. The depth of a child is
  read from its own journal, so a child of depth one does not look like a root
  after a restart and is refused the delegation that would put the grandchild
  at the depth two, when the agent of the child allows the depth one
  (lib/yeah-delegate.el, lib/yeah-subagent.el, lib/yeah-events.el; the claims
  `a-child-is-found-after-the-harness-restarts' and
  `a-session-knows-its-depth-from-the-journal'; docs/PLAN.md §16.20).
  Not implemented: a child that was running when the Emacs died is not
  brought back to life — the work of that child is lost.
- Wave 38 made the pilot name the shape of a run that did not finish: the
  reason of the row begins with what the journal of the run holds — the model
  answered with an empty message N times, or it described its next step N
  times and called no tool — so that a reader of the pilot sees the cause of
  a failed check and not only its verdict.  The status of the row does not
  change: whether such a run is a failure of the agent or a run that was never
  measured is a decision of the owner (docs/PLAN.md §17.2), and the runner does
  not take it (bench/run-bench.el; the claim
  `the-pilot-names-the-shape-of-a-run-that-did-not-finish'; docs/PLAN.md
  §16.21).
- Wave 39 made the kernel supervise a run by default: the budget of the
  completion nudges is positive (`yeah-turn-default-max-nudges` is 3), so a run
  of Yeah is supervised unless the caller asks for no supervision at all (a
  budget of zero).  Before the change, the ACP route answered `end_turn` for a
  run in which the model had only described its next step — the wire said the
  work was done, and nothing had been done.  A run that spends its budget
  without an effect now ends in the state `failed`, and the ACP route answers
  it with the stop reason `refusal` (the claims
  `supervision-is-the-default' and
  `a-run-that-did-not-finish-is-not-a-success'; docs/PLAN.md §16.22).  The
  budget of a child of a delegation is a separate default and is still zero:
  that decision belongs to the owner (docs/PLAN.md §17.2).

  content block (the protocol says one block, and a client that checks the
  wire refuses an array), and the events of the pending queue of a session —
  `input_queued', `input_taken', `input_recovered', `input_withdrawn' — are
  not ACP at all.  They travel only to the client that asked for them: the
  client announces them in the `_meta' of its capabilities at `initialize',
  and a client that announces nothing is served plain ACP.  The editor of
  Yeah announces them and sees the queue.  The name of the extension, the
  version of the protocol and the way the announcement is read live in
  `lib/yeah-acp-vocabulary.el`, which both sides of Yeah require (the claims
  `the-wire-speaks-acp' and
  `the-queue-events-travel-where-they-were-asked-for'; docs/PLAN.md §16.23).

  it refused every `session/update' of Yeah, so the text of the agent never
  reached the timeline of the client.
- The shapes of the wire were not the whole of it: the text of the agent
  still did not reach the client, because the model of the live task answered
  only with the call of the `finish' tool and the `finish' tool was not
  projected at all.  A client that speaks ACP expects the words of the agent
  as the message of the agent, so the summary of a finished run travels as
  `agent_message_chunk', and the call of a tool carries what it was called
  with and what it returned (`rawInput' and `rawOutput'; the claims
  `the-answer-of-the-agent-reaches-the-client' and
  `a-tool-call-carries-its-input-and-its-output').  The arguments of a call
  are read back from their printed form as data and never as code.
- The words themselves were spoiled on the way out, and the live check in
  Paseo found it: the answer of the model reached the timeline of the agent
  and arrived as mojibake, while the journal of the session held the right
  text.  Emacs's `json-serialize' returns a unibyte string whose bytes are
  UTF-8, and `princ' of such a string makes Emacs read every byte as a
  character of Latin-1 and write the characters back as UTF-8 — every
  non-ASCII answer was written twice over.  The wire now writes the bytes of
  a message as they are (`lib/yeah-wire.el', `yeah-wire-print-line'), and both
  protocols that write to a stream use it (the claim
  `the-text-on-the-wire-is-the-text-the-model-wrote'; the check reads the
  bytes of a real server process, because a character set would answer a

  provider found four defects that no offline check had seen, because every
  offline check had been written by the same hand as the code.  A `bash'
  tool whose output ends in a byte that is not valid UTF-8 killed the whole
  Emacs process: the refusal of JSON arrived inside the sentinel of the
  process, where no handler of the turn stands, and the run left no record
  of itself (exit code 255).  The bytes arrive in two shapes, and both are
  now text: a unibyte string of bytes, and a multibyte string that holds a
  raw byte where the decoder of a process refused one (a character whose
  code is at or above #x3FFF00).  The text of the harness is decided in one
  place (`lib/yeah-text.el'), and a byte that is not text becomes the
  replacement character (the claim

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

## Current warnings for every agent

- This is a kernel prototype, not a usable coding product.
- The parity with other harnesses was piloted on 2026-11-15, and the
  difference the pilot found was a defect of the turn, not a difference of
  quality: after the results of the tool calls arrive, the model may answer
  with an empty message, and the turn took that as the end of the work and
  stopped without the effect (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot of the
  parity").  The defect is fixed (the claim
  `an-empty-answer-does-not-end-the-run'), and the pilot on the fixed turn
  moved one task of three; the nudge now carries the state of the work
  (the claim `a-silence-nudge-carries-the-state-of-the-work'), because the
  provider goes silent after every batch of tool results and the model was
  answering the nudge by starting the work over.  With that, Yeah passes
  two tasks of three and pi passes three.  The third task failed in the
  tools: the `read` of a file nobody has edited yet returns no tick, and
  the `edit` refused the tick the model guessed as stale although the file
  has not changed; wave 26 makes a guessed tick ignored rather than
  refused (the claim
  `a-guessed-tick-does-not-refuse-an-unchanged-file'), and that task of the
  pilot passes now.  The provider was overloaded for hours (HTTP 529 to both
  harnesses), so the pilot of 15:02 measured one task of three and two
  blocked runs: the runner records a run the provider stopped as **blocked**,
  neither a pass nor a failure (the claim
  `a-provider-failure-is-not-a-failure-of-the-agent').  The pilot of 15:39, on
  the code of wave 28, measured two tasks of three — Yeah passed both of them
  and pi passed all three — and the third was blocked, because the transport
  to the provider died.  The parity of that run is not measured either.  The
  pilot of 17:06, on the code of waves 30+31, measured one task of three for
  Yeah and two of three for pi: all three runs of Yeah ended `unfinished`,
  because the provider goes silent, and the one task that failed in the tools
  failed on the **version token** of the file — the model copied 58 of the 64
  characters of the digest and the edit refused the edit of a file that had
  not changed (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot that measured the copy of the
  version token").  The pilot of 17:23, on the code of wave 32, measured two
  tasks of three for Yeah and three of three for pi: the token of the file is
  short now, the read handed out twelve characters, and the tasks the model
  worked on passed.  The task that Yeah failed failed on the provider: the
  model announced the fix ("Fixing it to use floating-point division:") and
  called no tool (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot after the token became
  short").  The pilot of 2026-11-16 06:43–06:48, on the code of wave 33, measured
  two tasks of three for Yeah and three of three for pi, and the pilot of

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.

4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

## 18. The plan of the next waves

The owner named the order of the next waves on 2026-11-16 (az), after the
report on the readiness of Yeah for self-development and after the
integration with the orchestrator Paseo.  The decision is recorded by the
method as the judgment claim `the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves`
(a human review, not a machine verifier), and this section is the plan that
the decision refers to.  The order is by the price of the defect: the wave
that makes the verdict of the method unreadable goes first, and the wave that
opens the path from a model to a working program goes last.

The order of the next waves, named by the owner on 2026-11-16: **wave 41, wave 42, wave 43, wave 44.**

They are: wave 41 (the deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the
process of the server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave
44 (parallel children in a live turn).

One wave was executed before them: **wave 45** (2026-11-17), the repair of
the harness that the live test of the harness forced — a tool that returns
bytes that are not text took the whole Emacs process down, and the four
waves of this plan need a harness that lives to carry them (§16.24).  The
order named by the owner is unchanged: wave 41 is still the first of the
four.

Every wave below names the defect it removes, the claims it registers, the
control that has to bite, and the criteria that close it.  A wave that ends
without a control that bites is not a wave: it is a change of the code with
no evidence.

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control
  that bites every time (register `fact`, requirement: the check of the
  bridge).
- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the
  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

**The exit criteria.**
1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an
   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.
2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`
   claim and no `unknown` verdict.

**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It
repairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

1. The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is
   recorded in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools
   do not read it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the directory of
   the Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  In the live
   check the `bash` of the agent ran in the directory of the installation of
   the CLI of Paseo, not in the repository of the task.
2. The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
   session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is
   answered with `-32601`.
3. The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
   `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists.
4. The `tool_call` of the wire names the tool and carries what it was called
   with and what it returned (`rawInput` and `rawOutput`, since wave 40), but
   no `kind`: a client that renders the call of a tool by its kind — a read,
   an edit, a shell — sees the name of the tool and nothing else.  The
   arguments of a call are positional, so a client that looks for named
   fields (`path`, `oldText`, `query`) does not find them.

**What changes.**  The gaps are closed in the order of what the live
integration needs today: the `cwd` first, because the agent must work in the
repository of the task; then the `kind` of the call and its named arguments,
because the client must be able to show what the agent did; then
`session/set_mode`; then the model of the session; then the `mcpServers` of
the session, whose tools do not reach the model today.

**The claims.**  Each gap is a claim of its own, and the name of the claim is
the name of the gap: `a-session-runs-in-its-own-directory`,
`a-tool-call-carries-its-kind`, `a-tool-call-carries-named-arguments`,
`a-session-changes-its-permission-profile-over-the-wire`,
`a-session-changes-its-model-over-the-wire`,
`the-mcp-servers-of-a-session-reach-the-model`.

**The exit criteria.**
1. The check of the `cwd` sends a session into a temporary directory, and the
   tool of that session sees the temporary directory and not the directory of
   the process.
2. The plugin of Paseo runs a turn in the repository of the task, and the
   timeline of the client shows the kind of the call of the tool.
3. The wire answers `session/set_mode` and no longer answers `-32601`.

**The estimate.**  Two to three days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  The
wire of Yeah is ACP plus the one extension that was announced
(`yeah.queueEvents`); this wave adds no method that ACP does not have.

### 18.4 Wave 44 — parallel children in a live turn

**The defect.**  Several children in one turn of the parent work already: the
audit of wave 35 proved it, and the plan that said otherwise was wrong.  What
is not proven is a *live* turn of a parent with two children of a live
provider.  No child of a live provider has run on a model other than the
model of its parent, and the live checks do not exercise the delegation at
all: the benchmark gives its runs a fixed set of tools, and the delegation is
not among them.

**What changes.**  The live check grows a second child in the same turn of
the parent, and the offline check with a fake model becomes the claim that
the map binds — the live check lives outside the map, because it needs a
provider.

**The claims.**
- `two-children-run-in-one-turn-of-the-parent` — the claim of the map, with a
  fake model: two delegations in one turn of the parent give two children,
  both alive, and the turn of the parent goes on (the control refuses the
  second delegation: the check must fail).
- `a-child-runs-on-the-model-of-its-preset` — the model of a child is the
  model of the preset, and not the model of its parent (the control names
  another model in the preset: the child must run on it).

**The exit criteria.**
1. The offline check passes and its control bites.
2. The live check with a real provider shows two children in one turn of the
   parent, and the tree of the children in the journal holds both.

**The estimate.**  One to two days, and a key of the provider for the live
part.  **What this wave does not fix.**  The budget of the completion
supervision of a child is zero today, and that is a decision of the owner
(§17.2), not a defect of this wave.

### 18.5 What this plan does not decide

Three decisions of the owner stay open, and no wave above takes them:
- the threshold of the parity, and the final set of the tasks of the benchmark
  (`docs/PLAN.md` §13): until it is decided, the parity is not claimed
  anywhere, and the pilot stays a measurement;
- whether a run that the provider silenced is a failure of the agent or a run
  that was never measured: it changes the number of every pilot;
- the budget of the completion supervision of a child of a delegation: the
  default of the kernel is positive since wave 39, the default of the child is
  still zero.

Two more items of the open work (§17.1) are not in the order above and stay
where they are: the pilot again, with a larger set of tasks, when the
provider answers; and the pixel check, which waits for the owner to name the
place of the frame server.

### 18.6 How this plan is measured

- One run of the method per wave, and a new run only for a new reason.
- Every new claim names its control before its check is written, and the
  control is shown to bite by an assertion of the check — not by a crash of
  Emacs and not by an unreadable test.
- The verdict of the map is the verdict of the wave: a wave that ends in
  `unknown` is not finished, whatever the code looks like.
- The live checks stay outside the map: they need a provider, and a check that
  cannot run without a key is `blocked`, not `pass`.
- A claim that the owner decides (a judgment) is recorded with
  `mathc record`, and never by an edit of the code.

## 17. What is left, and who decides it

The work of waves 24–38 is closed and bound to fresh evidence.  What follows is
everything that is still open, written down in one place, so that nobody has
to reconstruct it from the history of the sessions.  The first list is work an
agent may do; the second list is the work only the owner may decide, and no
agent may decide it silently (`docs/PLAN.md` §13).

### 17.1 The open work of the code

**The delegation (Stage 7, after wave 36).**

- Several children in one turn of the parent work already: the audit of wave 35
  proved it, and the plan that said otherwise was wrong.  What is not proven is
  a *live* turn of a parent with two children of a live provider.
- The model of the child is the model of the preset, and the preset names it;
  no child of a live provider has run yet on a model other than the model of
  its parent.
- The depth of the tree of the children and the children of a run are in the
  journal since wave 37: the journal of the run holds the short id, the
  session and the depth of every child, and the journal of the child holds
  where the child stands in the tree.  A restart of the harness finds the
  child of a run again and tells what became of it, and a child that the
  journal holds no end of is not reported as a child that still works.
- A child that was running when the Emacs died is not brought back to life: the
  journal says that the child was delegated and what became of it, and the
  work of that child is lost, because nobody restarts it.
- The live checks do not exercise the delegation: the benchmark gives its runs
  a fixed set of tools, and the delegation is not among them.  The live
  evidence of a child that works is the fixed point, and that is one child and
  one task.
- The tools of the delegation are not in `yeah-builtins-specs` (the built-ins
  are the tools of the kernel, and the delegation is a tool of the product),
  so a reader of that list does not see them.

**The turn, and what the provider and the model do.**

- A model can end its turn with a message that announces an action and call no
  tool ("I'll look at the current state of calc.el.").  The harness cannot tell
  a promise of an action from an answer: the completion nudge fires when the
  model is silent and not when the model talks without acting.  Since wave 39 a
  run of the kernel is supervised by default, so such a model is nudged into
  the action; a model that spends the budget without an effect ends the run as
  a failed run, and the ACP route answers `refusal` and not `end_turn`.
- A caller that wants the old behaviour of the kernel (a run that ends as soon
  as the model answers with text) must now say so with an explicit budget of
  zero.  The default changed for every caller at once.
- A message that reports a finished work **and** announces the next step at
  the same time is a plan in part, and the harness does not see that part:
  `yeah-turn-plan-regexp` matches "I'll", "I will", "Let me", "Next I",
  "I'm going to" and "I am going to", so "All 15 tests pass.  Verifying the
  CLI end-to-end from a shell:" reads as a result.  The live coding run of
  wave 45 ended that way: the model announced a verification it never
  performed, and the run was completed.  The task was already done there, so
  the gap cost nothing; a task whose *last* step is the announced one would
  end as a completed run with the step missing.
- A run that ends on a text answer is a completed run even when the task
  asked for the tool `finish`: the live coding run of wave 45 was told to
  finish through `finish` and never called it.  The state of a run is
  therefore not a proof that the instructions of the task were followed; the
  check of the task is the arbiter.  Whether the kernel should require
  `finish` is a decision of the owner (§17.2).
- The budget of a child of a delegation is a separate default and is still
  zero: a child that only talks still ends as a completed child.  Whether a
  child that never calls `finish` is a failed child is a decision of the owner
  (§17.2).
- The provider answers with an empty message after a batch of tool results,
  with the status of a success (HTTP 200, `answer=""`).  Since wave 46 such a
  silence does not spend the budget of the nudges when the model has acted: the
  noise of the provider is not the refusal of the model, and a run that works
  must not be ended by it.  A model that never acts still ends, and the record
  of a run that did not finish says what the run did.
- The budget of the nudges is no longer a bound on the length of a run: it pays
  for the nudges that no effect answered, and a model that acts and then says
  nothing is not charged for the silence (wave 46).  The deadline of the run and
  the deadline of the request still bound it; a caller who wants a bound on the
  length of a run must set a deadline.
- The provider is overloaded for hours: HTTP 529 to both harnesses, a plain
  model call that answers with nothing now and then, and a transport that
  times out ("Curl failed with exit code 28").  A run that the provider stops
  is blocked and not a failure of the agent.
- A run that the provider *silences* and a run that the provider *fails* are
  not told apart by the runner of the benchmark: the silence is not an error
  record of the journal, so the runner records it as a failure of the agent,
  and a run that was never measured counts against the agent.  The pilot of
  wave 36 and the pilot of wave 37 measured the third task of Yeah in that
  shape (the sum was computed, the file was never written).  Whether that
  shape is a failure of the agent or a run that was never measured is a
  decision of the owner (§17.2), because it changes the number of every
  pilot (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the pilot after wave
  37").
- The reason of the row of such a run names the shape of it since wave 38:
  the model answered with an empty message N times, or it described its next
  step N times and called no tool.  The shape is what the journal of the run
  holds, and the verdict of the row is still the verdict.
- The outcome of a run does not describe the work that was done: a run of
  `fix-failing-test` ended in "failed" because the provider failed after the
  edit, while the check of the task passed.  The check of the benchmark is the
  arbiter.

**The product.**

- A real editor (an agent-shell, or a person's Emacs) against a live provider:
  not yet checked.  The ACP agent and the MCP server are driven by a
  third-party client with a fake model, and the service path itself is
  verified with a live provider.
- The service path has no mode changes of the attached path and no opening of
  an earlier session by name.
- The bridge to the buffers of an attached Emacs is verified against a live
  Emacs server (a real daemon), and not against a person's Emacs in day-to-day
  use.
- The stdio server answers one request at a time: a cancel that arrives while
  a prompt is running is read after that prompt reaches a terminal state.  The
  socket transport does not have this limit.
- The picture of the interface is compared with itself and with the same
  buffer without the interface, and not with a stored golden picture.
- PTC stays an experimental, off-by-default restricted evaluator, and not a
  security boundary.

**The ACP surface, as an orchestrator sees it.**  The gaps below were found by
the integration with Paseo (docs/PASEO-INTEGRATION.md) and are still open.

- The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is recorded
  in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools do not read
  it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the working directory of the
  Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  An orchestrator
  that asks for a run in a repository gets a run in the directory of the
  service.
- The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
  session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is answered
  with `-32601`.
- The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
  `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists, so an
  orchestrator cannot choose the model of a run.
- The `mcpServers` of a session are ignored: the tools of an MCP server that a
  client names do not reach the model.
- The `tool_call` of the wire names the tool and carries what it was called
  with and what it returned (`rawInput` and `rawOutput`), but no `kind`: a
  client that renders the call of a tool by its kind — a read, an edit, a
  shell — sees the name of the tool and nothing else.  The arguments of a
  call are positional, so a client that looks for named fields (`path`,
  `oldText`, `query`) does not find them.
- The process of the server outlives the agent.  A client that keeps the pipe
  of the server open after the last turn leaves an Emacs process alive, and
  some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace: one
  of them was measured with 1.9 million involuntary context switches and six
  voluntary ones, and it never slept.  The read loop of the server is not the
  cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
  and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
  per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request
  of the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet.  The client that
  leaves the process behind is the plugin that spawned it: nothing closes the
  pipe of the server when the session of the agent is over.

**The measurement.**

- The pilot is three tasks.  The sample is small, and the numbers of the runs
  of waves 33, 34, 35, 36, 37 and 38 (2 of 3, 1 of 3, 2 of 3 and one blocked,
  2 of 3, 2 of 3) differ by the noise of the provider and of the model.
- The second harness is `pi` 1.1.0, which is checked in the environment;
  `opencode` is not installed here.
- One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The check of
  `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a hundred
  and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails only
  when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence bound that claim
  on 2026-11-16: five bit, and one did not — the control reached the
  subject, the verifier after the control still passed, the claim came out
  `inconclusive`, and the map came out `unknown`.  A claim whose control does
  not always bite is not established: until the check of that race is
  deterministic, the verdict of the map can be `unknown` for a reason that has
  nothing to do with the code it names.  The claim itself is not weakened
  here, and nobody may quote it as established on the strength of the runs
  where the race happened.

### 17.2 The decisions of the owner

None of these may be decided by an agent.  Each of them is recorded with

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

# Разбор сессии `6738289f` и план дальнейших работ

Документ отвечает на вопрос «что произошло в последней сессии агента и что делать
дальше». Написан 2026-11-15 после закрытия сессии `6738289f` и волны 21.

## 1. Что именно разбиралось

| | |
|---|---|
| Сессия | `6738289f-340a-4cb7-9a91-a556df563c70` (Paseo, провайдер `mcode`, модель MiniMax-M3) |
| Внутренний id | `mvs_36e1e7c30fb0490296b4d645e5996126` |
| Рабочий каталог | `/home/az/Projects/yeah` |
| Время | 2026-11-15, 07:57–12:17 UTC |
| Транскрипт | `~/.minimax/v2/sessions/2026/11/15/07-57-36-273-.../messages.jsonl` (3.5 МБ, 1376 записей) |
| Объём | 7 ходов, 668 вызовов инструментов, 342 блока размышления |
| Состояние на финише | `lastStatus: closed`, `lastError: "A foreground turn is already active"`, `requiresAttention: true` |

Предыдущая сессия — kimi-сессия `f4932812` (12–15 ноября). Она уже разобрана в
`docs/REVIEW-2026-11-15.md`; волна 21 — это исполнение того плана. Настоящий
разбор берёт следующий шаг: **что сделала сессия 15 ноября, чем это
подтверждается и что осталось за её пределами**.

## 2. Хронология сессии

| Время | Событие |
|---|---|
| 07:57 | Реплика человека: «Анализ сессии Emacs-агента … напиши план работы. Проверь выводы» |
| 08:15 | Реплика человека: «Реализуй согласно плану. Используй параллельные субагенты … используя агента дискриминатора для проверки» |
| 08:15–09:30 | Пять параллельных воркеров (P1, P2a, P2b+P4, P2c, P5) и верификатор-дискриминатор |
| 09:07 | Создана `waves/wave-21.json` (7 новых claim'ов) |
| 09:18 | Создан `docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md` — реестр живых доказательств |
| 09:27 | Создан `bench/` — 10 задач, манифест, раннер |
| 09:16 | Дискриминатор нашёл три дефекта: двойная запись steering'а в журнал, «catch-all» в `M-x yeah`, ошибка вместо `{"started": false}` в `session/recover` |
| 10:26 | Реплика человека: «Проанализируй, не слишком ли долго идут сборки и проверки … ускоряйся» |
| 10:32–10:40 | `scripts/dev` учится печатать время каждой проверки; локальные ожидания сокращены с 10–20 с до 4–8 с |
| 11:49 | `spec.json`: 74 claim'а (было 67) |
| 11:57 | Обновлён `docs/REVIEW-2026-11-15.md` разбором скорости проверок |
| 12:01 | Последняя содержательная реплика ассистента: карта зелёная, 74/74 контроля кусаются, 51 путь не закоммичен |
| 12:17 | Сессия закрыта ошибкой `A foreground turn is already active`. **Финального ответа человек не получил** |

Инструменты сессии: 290 `bash`, 178 `task_output`, 66 `read`, 52 `edit`,
32 `grep`, 12 `todowrite`, 9 `glob`, 9 `write`, 8 `task` (субагенты),
4 `tool_search`, 4 `mcp_invoke`, 2 `task_query`, 1 `skill`, 1 `task_append`.

## 3. Что сессия сделала хорошо

1. **План превращён в волну с проверяемыми claim'ами.** Семь новых claim'ов
   волны 21 зарегистрированы в `spec.json`; у каждого — требование, фальсификатор
   и отрицательный контроль, который ломает предмет.
2. **Параллельность использована по назначению.** Пять воркеров на непересекающихся
   кусках и отдельный верификатор-дискриминатор; найдено три настоящих дефекта.
3. **Документация приведена в соответствие с кодом.** `README.md`,
   `AGENTS.md`, `docs/PLAN.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` описывают новое поведение —
   асинхронный ответчик, контроль по проводу, сервис как путь по умолчанию,
   TCP-путь для платформ без Unix-сокетов.
4. **Найдена и устранена причина долгих проверок.** Сами проверки быстрые
   (byte-compile 2.9 с, 358 ERT 5.5 с, 53 канарейки 58 с, bench 2.3 с); время съедала
   **фаза отрицательных контролей** — 420 с против 287 с на проверки, и семь
   claim'ов давали из этих 420 с почти все 227 с. Таймауты сокращены вдвое-втрое.
5. **Честный реестр живых доказательств.** Шесть живых проверок вынесены из карты
   и описаны в `docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md`: у них нет отрицательного контроля, поэтому
   зелёный вердикт карты о них не говорит ничего.

## 4. Где сессия ослабила дисциплину

1. **Четверть вызовов — ожидание, а не работа.** 178 `task_output` плюс около 40
   циклов `sleep`/`pgrep` наблюдали за прогоном `mathc`. Сессия получила
   напоминание системы «три подряд чтения одной фоновой задачи — прекратите опрос»
   — и всё равно продолжала опрашивать.
2. **Метод прогонялся многократно.** За сессию гейт/прогон запускался минимум пять
   раз (`v1`, `v2`, `v3`, «final», «timed final», «solo») — два-три часа на один
   и тот же результат. Причины: два нерабочих контроля и наивный чекер, который
   трактовал шаблон `sed` как регулярку, а не как литерал.
3. **Сессия закрылась без ответа.** Ошибка `A foreground turn is already active`
   оставила человека без вердикта, хотя работа была сделана и проверена.
4. **Ничего не зафиксировано в git.** 51 путь волны (40 изменённых, 11 новых) остались
   в рабочем дереве: `docs/REVIEW-2026-11-15.md`, `docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md`,
   `waves/wave-21.json`, `bench/`, семь новых проверок, 1235 строк в ядре, схеме и
   скриптах, 640 строк в тестах и 294 строки в документации.
5. **Дефект структуры отчёта:** в `docs/REVIEW-2026-11-15.md` два раздела с
   номером «6» (строки 226 и 256) — нумерация сломана.
6. **Открытые пункты не разделены по природе блокировки.** §16.6 «пиксельный
   smoke» подан как «ждёт виртуальный frame server», хотя `Xvfb`/`xvfb-run` в
   окружении просто отсутствуют — это блокер окружения, а не «работа на потом».
7. **Реестр живых доказательств устарел относительно дерева:** все шесть записей
   датированы 2026-11-14, то есть до изменений 15 ноября.

## 5. Проверка выводов сессии

Проверено независимо, 2026-11-15, на текущем рабочем дереве.

| Утверждение сессии | Как проверено | Итог |
|---|---|---|
| Ядро компилируется без предупреждений | `./scripts/dev byte-compile-all` | exit 0 |
| 358 ERT-тестов проходят | `./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el` | 358/358, 6.8 с |
| 53 канарейки проходят | `./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*` | 53 файла, 56.1 с, exit 0 |
| Карта зелёная, 74 claim'а | `./scripts/dev map` | `verdict: green`, 74 `holds (current)`, 22 uncovered |
| Bench не выдумывает успех | `./scripts/dev bench` | 10/10 задач: check падает на нетронутом workspace; без провайдера — `skipped`, не `pass` |
| 7 новых claim'ов зарегистрированы с контролями | чтение `spec.json` и `waves/wave-21.json` | у всех есть требование, фальсификатор и контроль |
| Отрицательные контроли волны 21 действительно кусаются | каждая проверка запущена в изолированной копии дерева, куда применён её контроль | 7 из 7: проверка падает на сломанном предмете |
| Полный гейт (`run` + `map`) зелёный | `./scripts/dev gate` (отдельный процесс, 12:41:22–12:47:21 UTC) | `verdict: green`, `GATE_EXIT=0`, 359 с; 74 claim'а `holds (current)`; 74 из 74 контролей сработали; 51 проверка выполнена, ни одна не пропущена и не заблокирована; 23 uncovered-файла |
| Метод на месте | `mathc --version` | `mathc 5`, build `3d70f836` |

**Что подтвердилось:** карта зелёная, claim'ы держатся, код компилируется, тесты и
канарейки проходят, bench честен, документация соответствует коду. Свежие
доказательства записаны в `.math/v5/evidence.jsonl`: по 74 новые записи, все с
`outcome=pass`, `control_reach=subject`, `independence=fresh-context`.

**Одно замечание к методу (не к этой волне).** Контроль claim'а
`lib-byte-compiles-clean` обрезает `lib/yeah-state.el`, поэтому проверка падает
по ошибке разбора, а не по утверждению о предупреждениях. Свойство «компилируется
чисто» при этом всё равно опровергается — но автору метода стоит решить, считает
ли он такой контроль честным.

**Что осталось непроверенным:** живые пути (нужен ключ провайдера), реальный
редактор против живого провайдера, пиксельный интерфейс, паритет с opencode/pi.

## 6. Что осталось открытым по существу

| Пункт | Природа блокировки |
|---|---|
| §16.6 — пиксельный smoke | нет `Xvfb`/`xvfb-run` в окружении; Emacs 30.2 собран с GTK/X11, значит путь через виртуальный frame server реалистичен (dev-only зависимость) |
| §16.7 — измерение паритета | нужны живой провайдер, второй harness и решение владельца о пороге |
| Реальный редактор против живого провайдера | нужен провайдер и окружение редактора |
| Тик файла против D5 | **закрыто волной 29 (2026-11-15):** каждое чтение отдаёт вместе с тиком токен версии файла (дайджест его байтов), правка проверяет токен и отказывает, если файл изменился после чтения; D5 дополнена, а не ослаблена — вторым видом состояния (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §D5, `docs/PLAN.md` §16.12) |
| Чтение показывает диск, а тик описывает буфер | **закрыто волной 33 (2026-11-15):** правка файла, который Emacs держит с несохранёнными изменениями, отказывается всегда — с версией и без неё, потому что чтение идёт с диска и не может показать изменения человека; `write` принимает ту же короткую версию и отказывается, если файл изменился после чтения (`docs/PLAN.md` §16.16) |
| Открытие файла правкой | **закрыто волной 34 (2026-11-16):** правка открывает файл через `yeah-untrusted-open-file` (`lib/yeah-untrusted.el`), где `enable-local-variables`, `enable-local-eval` и `enable-dir-local-variables` связаны в nil: локальные переменные файла и `.dir-locals.el` каталога не исполняются, какой бы конфигурацией ни обладал этот Emacs. Цена названа: строка `-*- mode -*-` — часть содержимого файла, поэтому она игнорируется, и буфер показывает файл в режиме по имени (`docs/PLAN.md` §16.17) |
| Решение, отброшенное как повтор | **закрыто волной 30 (2026-11-15):** отброшенный повтор пишется в журнал событием `tool-dropped` (инструмент, причина, аргументы), и читатель журнала отличает повтор от решения, которого не было. Открытым остаётся то, что модель не уведомляется об отказе, а тождество вызова по-прежнему — инструмент плюс аргументы (`docs/PLAN.md` §16.13) |
| Lock-файлы Emacs рядом с журналом | **закрыто волной 31 (2026-11-15):** проверки читают журналы через общий читатель, который пропускает lock-файлы (`.#`) и переживает файл, исчезнувший между поиском и чтением. До этого проверка постоянных прав падала падением Emacs, а не своим утверждением, и claim'а была `inconclusive` (`docs/PLAN.md` §16.14) |
| Токен версии, который модель переписывает | **закрыто волной 32 (2026-11-15):** токен версии короче — 12 символов дайджеста вместо 64 — а отказ правки называет токен, а не файл, и сообщает текущий токен файла, чтобы повтор прошёл. Пилот 17:06 показал: модель переписала 58 символов из 64, и правка отказала на файле, который не менялся (`docs/PLAN.md` §16.15) |
| Реестр живых доказательств | **закрыто волнами 33–38:** шесть живых проверок и пилот перезапущены на коде волны 38 (2026-11-16, 13:10–13:12) и записаны в `docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md`; четыре из шести проверок прошли с первой попытки, две — со второй, и каждый провал был на провайдере. Пилот волны 38: Yeah — 1 из 3, pi — 3 из 3 |
| Провал прогона и провал агента | **открыто (найдено пилотом волны 36, повторено пилотами волн 37 и 38):** раннер бенчмарка отличает прогон, который провайдер остановил (запись `error` в журнале), от прогона, который провайдер *замолчал* (HTTP 200 и пустой ответ). Молчание попадает в «провал агента», хотя работа не была закончена: пилоты волн 36, 37 и 38 измерили задачи Yeah именно так (сумма посчитана, файл не записан). Волной 38 строка такого прогона называет форму («модель ответила пустым сообщением N раз, прогон закончился без действия»), но статус строки не меняется: решение — провал это или непомеренный прогон — меняет число каждого пилота и остаётся за владельцем (`docs/PLAN.md` §17.2) |
| Декларативная делегация (Stage 7) | **закрыто волнами 35–37:** модель родителя просит ребёнка инструментом `delegate`, который называет пресет агента; ребёнок работает в сессии своей, на модели пресета, с инструментами пресета и с инструкциями пресета, и любой инструмент вне пресета отказан ему. Ход родителя не держится: `delegate` отвечает сразу идентификатором ребёнка, ребёнок отвечает сам, `delegate-result` сообщает исход. Делегация меняет мир, поэтому Plan-профиль её запрещает (`docs/PLAN.md` §16.18). Аудит волны 35 нашёл дефект: делегация искала журнал через очередь запомненных сессий и могла попасть в журнал чужого прогона; волной 36 сессия прогона связывается с вызовом инструмента, и делегация пишется в журнал своего прогона (`docs/PLAN.md` §16.19). Волной 37 дерево детей перенесено в журнал: журнал прогона несёт короткий id, сессию и глубину каждого ребёнка, журнал ребёнка — своё место в дереве; перезапуск харнесса находит ребёнка прогона и говорит, чем он кончился, а ребёнок без записи об исходе не объявляется работающим (`docs/PLAN.md` §16.20). Открытым остаётся: ребёнок, работавший в момент смерти Emacs, не воскрешается — его работа теряется |
| Решения владельца (`docs/PLAN.md` §13, полный список — §17.2) | минимальные версии Emacs/gptel и цикл релизов; доступ сервиса к личным буферам; каналы и подпись пакетов; порог паритета и финальный набор задач бенчмарка; политика unattended-команд и сети; совместимость Apache-2.0; место frame server; приоритет следующей волны |

## 7. План дальнейших работ

### P0. Зафиксировать волну 21 (0.5–1 дня) — делать первым

**Сделано 2026-11-15:** волна разбита на семь коммитов, дерево чистое,
`./scripts/dev run` → exit 0, карта зелёная, 74 `holds (current)`.

Wave 40 repairs both shapes: the content of a chunk is one content block, as the schema of the wire says, and the events of the queue are an extension that travels only to the client that asked for them in the `_meta' of its capabilities at `initialize'.  The name of the extension, the version of the protocol and the way the announcement is read live in one file, `lib/yeah-acp-vocabulary.el', which both sides of Yeah require.  The second half of the wave answers the question the first half left open: the shapes of the wire were right, and the text of the agent still did not reach the client.  The model of the live task answered only with the call of the `finish' tool, the `finish' tool was not projected at all, and the client saw a `tool_call' without a word of the answer in it.  A client that speaks ACP expects the words of the agent as the message of the agent, so the summary of a finished run is projected as `agent_message_chunk', and the call of a tool carries what it was called with and what it returned (`rawInput' and `rawOutput').  The journal holds the arguments of a call in their printed form, so the printed form is read back into the values themselves — and, because the arguments come from the model, it is read as data and never as code.  The third part of the wave answers the question the second half left open: the text of the agent reached the client — the live check in Paseo showed the answer of the model in the timeline of the agent — and the words of it were mojibake.   the process, not in the repository of the task (docs/PLAN.md §17.1).
- The live stand of the transport was at fault, and not the provider: it stopped
  waiting at the first line that arrived, and the empty string that a
  reasoning model sends between its thinking and its answer was the absence of
  an answer.  The decision what counts as an answer now lives in
  tests/support/yeah-live-answer.el and is tested offline — text with content
  and a tool call are answers, the empty string, the streaming sentinel and the
  reasoning are not (the claim `the-live-stand-waits-for-an-answer').
- Stage 6 is implemented offline: the run context owns the session, the
  transport, the answerer and the rules of one run, and the three
  placements — attached, service, batch — write the same events for the
  same task. The bridge to the buffers of an attached Emacs is off until
  the operator turns it on; it is checked against a live Emacs server
  (a real daemon) by tests/checks/check-bridge-live-server.el.
- Stage 5 is implemented offline: the ACP agent and the MCP server speak
  newline JSON-RPC over stdio and over a local socket, the `emacs__*`
  handlers are real, and the MCP client imports foreign tools. The wire is
  now driven by a third-party client (xenodium/acp.el) with a fake model;
  the service path with a live provider is covered by
  tests/live/live-service-path.el;
  what is still not proven is a real editor against a live provider.  Two
  limits are not hidden — the stdio server answers one request at a time
  (a blocking stdin read stops the event loop, so a cancel cannot preempt
  a running prompt there; the socket transport can), and a live provider
  has not driven the MCP server.
- REPL still contains placeholders. Do not build new public behavior on
  top of it while its stage's prerequisites are unmet.
- Stage 4 is implemented offline and verified against a live provider:
  `M-x yeah`, journal commands, the Org export, doctor and a package-vc
  bootstrap exist.  A real model (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash) finishes the Stage 1 coding
  task, and the interactive path works against a live provider.  The
  clean-Emacs install path is network-tested against the published
  repository (tests/live/live-clean-install.el): the public alpha gate is
  closed; v0.2.0 carries the Emacs-native interface.
- The interface is seen, not only described: `tests/pixel/` draws the journal
  and the approval view in Emacs itself under a virtual frame server and
  photographs the screen; `./scripts/dev pixel` compares the pictures with
  each other and with the same buffer without the interface.  It needs a
  frame server, a terminal emulator and ImageMagick but no provider key, so
  it lives outside the map — like the live checks — and is registered in
  `docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md`.  A stored golden picture is still open.
- Stage 3 is implemented offline: the Plan and Build permission profiles,
  a persistent pending FIFO, frozen inputs,
  steering at batch boundaries, cancellation, nudges and deadlines have
  integration tests, including synchronous callback races. The journey of a
  person — ask, steer, quit, restart, withdraw, recover, cancel — is checked
  end to end with a fake model.
- Stage 2 is implemented offline: usage calibration, asynchronous compaction,
  pruning events and corrupt-tail recovery are covered by unit/canary tests.
  The compatibility `yeah-context-summarize` never waits; real providers use
  the asynchronous API. Live-provider acceptance remains unverified.
- Stage 1 is implemented offline: coding tools, tick editing, async jobs,
  output artifacts and Emacs introspection pass their unit and end-to-end
  checks. Live-provider acceptance has not been verified.
- Stage 0.5 is implemented: module comments match current behavior and no
  longer reference nonexistent decisions/Tier/ROADMAP documents. Stage 0.4
  is implemented: the project migrated to math-coding v5; `mathc run`, `map`
  and `gate` work with the installed v5 binary.
- Stage 0.3 is implemented: tool failures are bounded, model-facing results
  are strings, and duplicate async callbacks cannot settle a call twice.
- Stage 0.2 is implemented: PTC is disabled by default and the demonstrated
  higher-order-function bypasses have regression tests. It remains an
  experimental restricted evaluator, never a sandbox for untrusted code.
- Stage 0.1 is implemented: gptel requests use a private, version-checked
  adapter without global hooks. Recheck compatibility whenever gptel changes;
  supported pinned versions are declared in `lib/yeah-gptel.el`.
- A `holds` claim proves its stated check only, not overall product readiness.
- The owner named the order of the next waves on 2026-11-16 (az): wave 41
  (the deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the process of the
  server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave 44 (parallel
  children in a live turn).  The plan is `docs/PLAN.md` §18, and the decision
  is recorded by the method as the judgment claim
  `the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves` — a claim whose evidence is
  a human review, not a machine verifier.  Three decisions of the owner stay
  open, and no agent may take them: the threshold of the parity, the
  classification of a run that the provider silenced, and the budget of the
  supervision of a child (`docs/PLAN.md` §17.2, §18.5).
- Everything that is still open is written down in one place:
  `docs/PLAN.md` §17 — the work an agent may do, the decisions only the owner
  may make (§17.2), and the order to follow when the owner says nothing
  (§17.3).  Read it before starting the next wave; do not resolve an owner
  decision silently.

## The commands

```sh
./scripts/dev help                  # the list of subcommands
./scripts/dev byte-compile-all      # kernel compiles clean, with no warnings
./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el   # unit tests
./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*  # canaries bound to claims
./scripts/dev map                   # claims, states and uncovered surface
./scripts/dev run                   # execute checks and bind evidence
./scripts/dev gate                  # run, then map; exit code is the verdict
# Opt-in real model call; credentials come from the environment:
emacs -Q --batch -L lib -l tests/live/live-model-call.el
```

`scripts/dev` needs Emacs on `PATH` (or `EMACS`). Method commands also need a
compatible math-coding binary on `PATH` or in `MATHC`. A CLI/version mismatch
is blocked tooling, not a successful check.

Exit codes are: `0` pass, `1` fail, `2` blocked/input error and `3` unknown.
Unknown is never pass.

## The method

Start with the map when the compatible method binary is available:

```sh
./scripts/dev map
```

A claim has a scope, requirement, falsifier, register and **control**. The
control breaks the subject and must make the check fail by a real assertion,
not merely by making the test unreadable or crashing Emacs. A claim whose
control has not bitten is not established.

Two rules are not negotiable:

- **A check that cannot fail is a comment.**
- **Unknown is not pass.**

A placeholder that returns success is also a failed implementation. Public
scenarios must be tested end to end, not inferred from the presence of a
function or module.
