## 18. The plan of the next waves

The owner named the order of the next waves on 2026-11-16 (az), after the
report on the readiness of Yeah for self-development and after the
integration with the orchestrator Paseo.  The decision is recorded by the
method as the judgment claim `the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves`
(a human review, not a machine verifier), and this section is the plan that
the decision refers to.  The order is by the price of the defect: the wave
that makes the verdict of the method unreadable goes first, and the wave that
opens the path from a model to a working program goes last.

The order of the next waves, named by the owner on 2026-11-16: **wave 41, wave 42, wave 43, wave 44.**

They are: wave 41 (the deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the
process of the server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave
44 (parallel children in a live turn).

One wave was executed before them: **wave 45** (2026-11-17), the repair of
the harness that the live test of the harness forced — a tool that returns
bytes that are not text took the whole Emacs process down, and the four
waves of this plan need a harness that lives to carry them (§16.24).  The
order named by the owner is unchanged: wave 41 is still the first of the
four.

Every wave below names the defect it removes, the claims it registers, the
control that has to bite, and the criteria that close it.  A wave that ends
without a control that bites is not a wave: it is a change of the code with
no evidence.

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control
  that bites every time (register `fact`, requirement: the check of the
  bridge).
- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the
  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

**The exit criteria.**
1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an
   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.
2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`
   claim and no `unknown` verdict.

**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It
repairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

1. The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is
   recorded in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools
   do not read it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the directory of
   the Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  In the live
   check the `bash` of the agent ran in the directory of the installation of
   the CLI of Paseo, not in the repository of the task.
2. The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
   session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is
   answered with `-32601`.
3. The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
   `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists.
4. The `tool_call` of the wire names the tool and carries what it was called
   with and what it returned (`rawInput` and `rawOutput`, since wave 40), but
   no `kind`: a client that renders the call of a tool by its kind — a read,
   an edit, a shell — sees the name of the tool and nothing else.  The
   arguments of a call are positional, so a client that looks for named
   fields (`path`, `oldText`, `query`) does not find them.

**What changes.**  The gaps are closed in the order of what the live
integration needs today: the `cwd` first, because the agent must work in the
repository of the task; then the `kind` of the call and its named arguments,
because the client must be able to show what the agent did; then
`session/set_mode`; then the model of the session; then the `mcpServers` of
the session, whose tools do not reach the model today.

**The claims.**  Each gap is a claim of its own, and the name of the claim is
the name of the gap: `a-session-runs-in-its-own-directory`,
`a-tool-call-carries-its-kind`, `a-tool-call-carries-named-arguments`,
`a-session-changes-its-permission-profile-over-the-wire`,
`a-session-changes-its-model-over-the-wire`,
`the-mcp-servers-of-a-session-reach-the-model`.

**The exit criteria.**
1. The check of the `cwd` sends a session into a temporary directory, and the
   tool of that session sees the temporary directory and not the directory of
   the process.
2. The plugin of Paseo runs a turn in the repository of the task, and the
   timeline of the client shows the kind of the call of the tool.
3. The wire answers `session/set_mode` and no longer answers `-32601`.

**The estimate.**  Two to three days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  The
wire of Yeah is ACP plus the one extension that was announced

### 18.4 Wave 44 — parallel children in a live turn

**The defect.**  Several children in one turn of the parent work already: the
audit of wave 35 proved it, and the plan that said otherwise was wrong.  What
is not proven is a *live* turn of a parent with two children of a live
provider.  No child of a live provider has run on a model other than the
model of its parent, and the live checks do not exercise the delegation at

not among them.

**What changes.**  The live check grows a second child in the same turn of
the parent, and the offline check with a fake model becomes the claim that

**The claims.**

  output artifacts and Emacs introspection pass their unit and end-to-end
  checks. Live-provider acceptance has not been verified.
- Stage 0.5 is implemented: module comments match current behavior and no
  longer reference nonexistent decisions/Tier/ROADMAP documents. Stage 0.4
  is implemented: the project migrated to math-coding v5; `mathc run`, `map`
  and `gate` work with the installed v5 binary.
- Stage 0.3 is implemented: tool failures are bounded, model-facing results
  are strings, and duplicate async callbacks cannot settle a call twice.
- Stage 0.2 is implemented: PTC is disabled by default and the demonstrated
  higher-order-function bypasses have regression tests. It remains an
  experimental restricted evaluator, never a sandbox for untrusted code.
- Stage 0.1 is implemented: gptel requests use a private, version-checked
  adapter without global hooks. Recheck compatibility whenever gptel changes;
  supported pinned versions are declared in `lib/yeah-gptel.el`.
- A `holds` claim proves its stated check only, not overall product readiness.
- The owner named the order of the next waves on 2026-11-16 (az): wave 41
  (the deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the process of the
  server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave 44 (parallel
  children in a live turn).  The plan is `docs/PLAN.md` §18, and the decision
  is recorded by the method as the judgment claim
  `the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves` — a claim whose evidence is
  a human review, not a machine verifier.  Three decisions of the owner stay
  open, and no agent may take them: the threshold of the parity, the
  classification of a run that the provider silenced, and the budget of the
  supervision of a child (`docs/PLAN.md` §17.2, §18.5).
- Everything that is still open is written down in one place:
  `docs/PLAN.md` §17 — the work an agent may do, the decisions only the owner
  may make (§17.2), and the order to follow when the owner says nothing
  (§17.3).  Read it before starting the next wave; do not resolve an owner
  decision silently.

## The commands

```sh
./scripts/dev help                  # the list of subcommands
./scripts/dev byte-compile-all      # kernel compiles clean, with no warnings
./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el   # unit tests
./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*  # canaries bound to claims
./scripts/dev map                   # claims, states and uncovered surface
./scripts/dev run                   # execute checks and bind evidence
./scripts/dev gate                  # run, then map; exit code is the verdict
# Opt-in real model call; credentials come from the environment:
emacs -Q --batch -L lib -l tests/live/live-model-call.el
```

`scripts/dev` needs Emacs on `PATH` (or `EMACS`). Method commands also need a
compatible math-coding binary on `PATH` or in `MATHC`. A CLI/version mismatch
is blocked tooling, not a successful check.

Exit codes are: `0` pass, `1` fail, `2` blocked/input error and `3` unknown.
Unknown is never pass.

## The method

Start with the map when the compatible method binary is available:

```sh
./scripts/dev map
```

A claim has a scope, requirement, falsifier, register and **control**. The
control breaks the subject and must make the check fail by a real assertion,
not merely by making the test unreadable or crashing Emacs. A claim whose
control has not bitten is not established.

Two rules are not negotiable:

- **A check that cannot fail is a comment.**
- **Unknown is not pass.**

A placeholder that returns success is also a failed implementation. Public
scenarios must be tested end to end, not inferred from the presence of a
function or module.

<!-- math-coding:begin -->
## math-coding in this project

Yeah is an Emacs Lisp agent harness: the harness runs in a dedicated Emacs process (the service placement); the model goes through gptel, every tool goes through the registry and the permission system, the session log stays append-only, and the editor reaches it through the bridge or an ACP/MCP client

106 claim(s).

```sh
mathc run
```

Every verb: mathc help mathc init mathc goal mathc add mathc run mathc map mathc next mathc context mathc waive mathc record mathc install mathc doctor mathc adopt mathc import-adr mathc import-junit mathc authorize mathc re-evaluate mathc review-source mathc mcp
<!-- math-coding:end -->

## Task recording for the Math Coding field pilot

This project takes part in a measurement of the method itself. A task that ends
with a handoff is recorded in the field lab; without that record the pilot has
no data and the method cannot be judged.

At the end of the task, create a draft — the machine fields are filled for you:

```sh
~/Projects/math-coding-field-lab/scripts/record draft yeah --kind <kind> --base <revision-at-task-start>
```

Fill the fields marked `TODO`: the model, the time, the counters. Leave `outcome`
as `pending` and `accepted_by` empty — the owner decides the outcome and records
the acceptance, and that is not the agent's call. Then write the record:

```sh
~/Projects/math-coding-field-lab/scripts/record commit yeah --task-id <id>
```

Rules: do not choose tasks by their result, do not rewrite a written record to
make it look better, and do not drop unsuccessful ones — the pilot publishes
every outcome. The lab records every task that starts after the declared rule:
it never stops asking and it never filters by result. If the lab is not
available, finish the task as usual: a missing record is a gap in the
measurement, not a reason to change the work.

## Working rules

- Follow the stage order in `docs/PLAN.md`; do not start ACP, placements or
  sub-agents ahead of their prerequisites.
- Every new claim needs a control shown to bite. Every feature needs an
  observable end-to-end check appropriate to its layer.
- `lib/` is Elisp only. No C, Rust or shell scripts inside the kernel.
- One feature per file; `(require 'yeah-x)` loads `lib/yeah-x.el`.
- Public symbols use `yeah-`; internal helpers use `yeah--` or the module's
  established internal prefix.
- Domain errors are `user-error` or structured tool errors, not false success.
- Use `let` for request-local dynamic configuration of special variables;
  use `setq` only for intended global/session mutation. See ELISP §11.1.
- Subprocesses use `make-process`, never blocking `shell-command` in tools.
- Interactive execution never waits by spinning the event loop.
- Run context, permissions and sessions must not leak through new global
  mutable state.
- No telemetry, secret logging, global default keybindings or global gptel
  mutation.
- Development-only Nix/mathc/research clones never become runtime dependencies.

The detailed rationale and additional rules are in `docs/ENGINEERING.md` and
`ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md`. Update documentation whenever behavior changes;
update `AGENTS.md` if the documented workflow itself changes.

# Разбор сессии `6738289f` и план дальнейших работ

Документ отвечает на вопрос «что произошло в последней сессии агента и что делать
дальше». Написан 2026-11-15 после закрытия сессии `6738289f` и волны 21.

## 1. Что именно разбиралось

| | |
|---|---|
| Сессия | `6738289f-340a-4cb7-9a91-a556df563c70` (Paseo, провайдер `mcode`, модель MiniMax-M3) |
| Внутренний id | `mvs_36e1e7c30fb0490296b4d645e5996126` |
| Рабочий каталог | `/home/az/Projects/yeah` |
| Время | 2026-11-15, 07:57–12:17 UTC |
| Транскрипт | `~/.minimax/v2/sessions/2026/11/15/07-57-36-273-.../messages.jsonl` (3.5 МБ, 1376 записей) |
| Объём | 7 ходов, 668 вызовов инструментов, 342 блока размышления |
| Состояние на финише | `lastStatus: closed`, `lastError: "A foreground turn is already active"`, `requiresAttention: true` |

Предыдущая сессия — kimi-сессия `f4932812` (12–15 ноября). Она уже разобрана в
`docs/REVIEW-2026-11-15.md`; волна 21 — это исполнение того плана. Настоящий
разбор берёт следующий шаг: **что сделала сессия 15 ноября, чем это
подтверждается и что осталось за её пределами**.

## 2. Хронология сессии

| Время | Событие |
|---|---|
| 07:57 | Реплика человека: «Анализ сессии Emacs-агента … напиши план работы. Проверь выводы» |
| 08:15 | Реплика человека: «Реализуй согласно плану. Используй параллельные субагенты … используя агента дискриминатора для проверки» |
| 08:15–09:30 | Пять параллельных воркеров (P1, P2a, P2b+P4, P2c, P5) и верификатор-дискриминатор |
| 09:07 | Создана `waves/wave-21.json` (7 новых claim'ов) |
| 09:18 | Создан `docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md` — реестр живых доказательств |
| 09:27 | Создан `bench/` — 10 задач, манифест, раннер |
| 09:16 | Дискриминатор нашёл три дефекта: двойная запись steering'а в журнал, «catch-all» в `M-x yeah`, ошибка вместо `{"started": false}` в `session/recover` |
| 10:26 | Реплика человека: «Проанализируй, не слишком ли долго идут сборки и проверки … ускоряйся» |
| 10:32–10:40 | `scripts/dev` учится печатать время каждой проверки; локальные ожидания сокращены с 10–20 с до 4–8 с |
| 11:49 | `spec.json`: 74 claim'а (было 67) |
| 11:57 | Обновлён `docs/REVIEW-2026-11-15.md` разбором скорости проверок |
| 12:01 | Последняя содержательная реплика ассистента: карта зелёная, 74/74 контроля кусаются, 51 путь не закоммичен |
| 12:17 | Сессия закрыта ошибкой `A foreground turn is already active`. **Финального ответа человек не получил** |

Инструменты сессии: 290 `bash`, 178 `task_output`, 66 `read`, 52 `edit`,
32 `grep`, 12 `todowrite`, 9 `glob`, 9 `write`, 8 `task` (субагенты),
4 `tool_search`, 4 `mcp_invoke`, 2 `task_query`, 1 `skill`, 1 `task_append`.

## 3. Что сессия сделала хорошо

1. **План превращён в волну с проверяемыми claim'ами.** Семь новых claim'ов
   волны 21 зарегистрированы в `spec.json`; у каждого — требование, фальсификатор
   и отрицательный контроль, который ломает предмет.
2. **Параллельность использована по назначению.** Пять воркеров на непересекающихся
   кусках и отдельный верификатор-дискриминатор; найдено три настоящих дефекта.
3. **Документация приведена в соответствие с кодом.** `README.md`,
   `AGENTS.md`, `docs/PLAN.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` описывают новое поведение —
   асинхронный ответчик, контроль по проводу, сервис как путь по умолчанию,
   TCP-путь для платформ без Unix-сокетов.
4. **Найдена и устранена причина долгих проверок.** Сами проверки быстрые
   (byte-compile 2.9 с, 358 ERT 5.5 с, 53 канарейки 58 с, bench 2.3 с); время съедала
   **фаза отрицательных контролей** — 420 с против 287 с на проверки, и семь
   claim'ов давали из этих 420 с почти все 227 с. Таймауты сокращены вдвое-втрое.
5. **Честный реестр живых доказательств.** Шесть живых проверок вынесены из карты
   и описаны в `docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md`: у них нет отрицательного контроля, поэтому
   зелёный вердикт карты о них не говорит ничего.

## 4. Где сессия ослабила дисциплину

1. **Четверть вызовов — ожидание, а не работа.** 178 `task_output` плюс около 40
   циклов `sleep`/`pgrep` наблюдали за прогоном `mathc`. Сессия получила
   напоминание системы «три подряд чтения одной фоновой задачи — прекратите опрос»
   — и всё равно продолжала опрашивать.
2. **Метод прогонялся многократно.** За сессию гейт/прогон запускался минимум пять
   раз (`v1`, `v2`, `v3`, «final», «timed final», «solo») — два-три часа на один
   и тот же результат. Причины: два нерабочих контроля и наивный чекер, который
   трактовал шаблон `sed` как регулярку, а не как литерал.
3. **Сессия закрылась без ответа.** Ошибка `A foreground turn is already active`
   оставила человека без вердикта, хотя работа была сделана и проверена.
4. **Ничего не зафиксировано в git.** 51 путь волны (40 изменённых, 11 новых) остались
   в рабочем дереве: `docs/REVIEW-2026-11-15.md`, `docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md`,
   `waves/wave-21.json`, `bench/`, семь новых проверок, 1235 строк в ядре, схеме и
   скриптах, 640 строк в тестах и 294 строки в документации.
5. **Дефект структуры отчёта:** в `docs/REVIEW-2026-11-15.md` два раздела с
   номером «6» (строки 226 и 256) — нумерация сломана.
6. **Открытые пункты не разделены по природе блокировки.** §16.6 «пиксельный
   smoke» подан как «ждёт виртуальный frame server», хотя `Xvfb`/`xvfb-run` в
   окружении просто отсутствуют — это блокер окружения, а не «работа на потом».
7. **Реестр живых доказательств устарел относительно дерева:** все шесть записей
   датированы 2026-11-14, то есть до изменений 15 ноября.

## 5. Проверка выводов сессии

Проверено независимо, 2026-11-15, на текущем рабочем дереве.

| Утверждение сессии | Как проверено | Итог |
|---|---|---|
| Ядро компилируется без предупреждений | `./scripts/dev byte-compile-all` | exit 0 |
| 358 ERT-тестов проходят | `./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el` | 358/358, 6.8 с |
| 53 канарейки проходят | `./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*` | 53 файла, 56.1 с, exit 0 |
| Карта зелёная, 74 claim'а | `./scripts/dev map` | `verdict: green`, 74 `holds (current)`, 22 uncovered |
| Bench не выдумывает успех | `./scripts/dev bench` | 10/10 задач: check падает на нетронутом workspace; без провайдера — `skipped`, не `pass` |
| 7 новых claim'ов зарегистрированы с контролями | чтение `spec.json` и `waves/wave-21.json` | у всех есть требование, фальсификатор и контроль |
| Отрицательные контроли волны 21 действительно кусаются | каждая проверка запущена в изолированной копии дерева, куда применён её контроль | 7 из 7: проверка падает на сломанном предмете |
| Полный гейт (`run` + `map`) зелёный | `./scripts/dev gate` (отдельный процесс, 12:41:22–12:47:21 UTC) | `verdict: green`, `GATE_EXIT=0`, 359 с; 74 claim'а `holds (current)`; 74 из 74 контролей сработали; 51 проверка выполнена, ни одна не пропущена и не заблокирована; 23 uncovered-файла |
| Метод на месте | `mathc --version` | `mathc 5`, build `3d70f836` |

**Что подтвердилось:** карта зелёная, claim'ы держатся, код компилируется, тесты и
канарейки проходят, bench честен, документация соответствует коду. Свежие
доказательства записаны в `.math/v5/evidence.jsonl`: по 74 новые записи, все с
`outcome=pass`, `control_reach=subject`, `independence=fresh-context`.

**Одно замечание к методу (не к этой волне).** Контроль claim'а
`lib-byte-compiles-clean` обрезает `lib/yeah-state.el`, поэтому проверка падает
по ошибке разбора, а не по утверждению о предупреждениях. Свойство «компилируется
чисто» при этом всё равно опровергается — но автору метода стоит решить, считает
ли он такой контроль честным.

**Что осталось непроверенным:** живые пути (нужен ключ провайдера), реальный
редактор против живого провайдера, пиксельный интерфейс, паритет с opencode/pi.

## 6. Что осталось открытым по существу

| Пункт | Природа блокировки |

The control of `the-record-of-a-run-that-did-not-finish-is-true' makes every unfinished record claim that the run ended without an effect, and the check fails on two assertions: the record does not name the tool the run called, and the record says that the run ended without an effect although it did not.  The check itself was wrong twice before it was right: the first version collected the failures into a list with nil in it, and a list of nils is not empty, so the check could not fail; the second version read the state of the run backwards and demanded `unfinished' from a run that had finished.  The wave also found a defect of its own reasoning before the check caught it: the first version of the repair treated every silence as the noise of the provider and made the budget of the nudges meaningless for a model that never acts.  A model that never acts still ends now, and the check of that case is part of the same file.  The wave broke the control of an old claim, and the map of the method caught it: the claim `nudge-only-for-plans' removed the condition `(and (< (yeah-turn-nudges turn) (yeah-turn-max-nudges turn))' from `lib/yeah-turn.el', and the wave replaced that condition with the count of the nudges that were spent (`yeah-turn-nudge-spent'), so the control of the claim changed nothing, the verifier of the claim passed with the subject unchanged, and the claim went `inconclusive'.  The control was written against the code of the wave -- it makes the condition of the spending branch unreachable -- and it bites again: four tests of `tests/unit/test-yeah-control.el' fail on their own assertions, the run that was nudged twice is nudged zero times.  An old control is a promise that the code it names is still there, and a wave that renames a condition breaks that promise without knowing it.  The live run that found the defect is in docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md."
}

commit ab3d89285f79ee2b1b7ab8f95d764e4e90377a7d
Author: opencode-agent <agent@opencode.local>
Date:   Sun Nov 15 12:56:01 2026 +0000

    test: the canaries wait less, and say how long they took
    
    The checks were not slow: the waiting was. Every deadline that only exists
    to give a slow machine room is now short enough to fail fast, and
    `scripts/dev check' prints the time each check took, so the next person
    does not have to guess where the wait was.
    
    The full method run takes about six minutes, most of it in the negative
    controls.

diff --git a/tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el b/tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el
index c4a4054..9a499e5 100644
--- a/tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el
+++ b/tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el
@@ -60,7 +60,7 @@ loss is certain without the fix.")
          :connection-type 'pipe
          :noquery t)
         ;; wait for the server
-        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 15)))
+        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 8)))
           (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
                       (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
                                     (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil

commit baecb167409a1fb99328f105a1cd5f249ee30669
Author: opencode-agent <agent@opencode.local>
Date:   Sat Nov 14 14:55:52 2026 +0000

    fix: the bridge no longer loses the answer of the attached Emacs
    
    The bridge collected what the attached Emacs printed with a process
    filter. A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the filter: the
    answer was then lost, and the bridge reported success with an empty
    output — the person saw an empty buffer that the server had never
    emptied. It showed up under load: the bridge check failed about one run
    in four, and math-coding refuted the claim.
    
    The bridge now drains the pending events after the exit until the output
    stops changing. New canary check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el reads the
    same live buffer a hundred and twenty times under a spinning thread and
    requires that no answer is ever empty; claim bridge-keeps-the-answer.

diff --git a/tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el b/tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..c4a4054
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el
@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el --- the bridge does not lose the answer -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
+;;
+;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
+;;
+;; This file is part of Yeah.
+;;
+;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
+;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.
+
+;;; Commentary:
+;;
+;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
+;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the filter:
+;; the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success with an empty
+;; output — the person saw an empty buffer that the server had never
+;; emptied.  This check reads the same live buffer many times through the
+;; bridge and requires that no answer is ever empty.
+
+;;; Code:
+
+(require 'cl-lib)
+(require 'yeah-bridge)
+
+(defvar yeah-check--emacs
+  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
+           (getenv "EMACS"))
+      (executable-find "emacs")
+      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
+  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")
+
+(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
+  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
+         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
+    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
+        (executable-find "emacsclient")
+        candidate))
+  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")
+
+(defvar yeah-check--reads 120
+  "How many times the check reads the buffer through the bridge.
+Losing an answer is a race between the exit of the child process and the
+delivery of its last chunk, so it shows up under load: the check keeps a
+thread spinning to make the parent late, and reads often enough that the
+loss is certain without the fix.")
+
+(defvar yeah-check--load-thread nil
+  "The thread that keeps the parent late, so the race can happen.")
+
+(let ((failures nil)
+      (name (format "yeah-bridge-keep-%d" (random 1000000)))
+      (empty 0))
+  (unwind-protect
+      (progn
+        (make-process
+         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"
+         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
+                        (concat "--daemon=" name)
+                        "--eval"
+                        "(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \"*yeah-live*\") (insert \"live text\"))")
+         :connection-type 'pipe
+         :noquery t)
+        ;; wait for the server
+        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 15)))
+          (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
+                      (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
+                                    (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil
+                                                  "-s" name "--eval" "t")))))
+            (accept-process-output nil 0.1)))
+        ;; a spinning thread makes the parent slow, which is when the
+        ;; answer of the child is lost
+        (setq yeah-check--load-thread
+              (make-thread
+               (lambda ()
+                 (let ((counter 0))
+                   (while (< counter 100000000)
+                     (setq counter (1+ counter)))))))
+        (dotimes (_ yeah-check--reads)
+          (let ((text (condition-case err
+                         (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
+                               (yeah-bridge-server name))
+                           (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
+                       (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))
+            (when (or (null text) (equal text ""))
+              (setq empty (1+ empty)))))
+        (when (> empty 0)
+          (push (format "the bridge lost the answer %d times out of %d"
+                        empty yeah-check--reads)
+                failures)))
+    (when yeah-check--load-thread
+      (ignore-errors (thread-signal yeah-check--load-thread 'quit)))
+    (ignore-errors
+      (with-temp-buffer
+        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil "-s" name "--eval" "(kill-emacs)"))))
+    (dolist (failure failures)
+      (message "bridge-keep: %s" failure))
+    (if failures
+        (kill-emacs 1)
+      (kill-emacs 0))))
+
+;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el ends here

Author: opencode-agent <agent@opencode.local>
Date:   Sat Nov 14 14:55:52 2026 +0000

    fix: the bridge no longer loses the answer of the attached Emacs
    
    The bridge collected what the attached Emacs printed with a process
    filter. A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the filter: the
    answer was then lost, and the bridge reported success with an empty
    output — the person saw an empty buffer that the server had never
    emptied. It showed up under load: the bridge check failed about one run
    in four, and math-coding refuted the claim.
    
    The bridge now drains the pending events after the exit until the output
    stops changing. New canary check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el reads the
    same live buffer a hundred and twenty times under a spinning thread and
    requires that no answer is ever empty; claim bridge-keeps-the-answer.

                   (ignore-errors (kill-process process)))
+                ;; A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
+                ;; filter: the answer of the attached Emacs is then lost
+                ;; and the bridge answers with nothing.  Draining the
+                ;; pending events after the exit — until the output stops

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

now_ms() {
  printf '%s' "$(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))"
}

case "$cmd" in
  help|--help|-h)
    cat <<'EOF'
scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper

Subcommands:
  smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
  byte-compile-all      — byte-compile lib/*.el (including lib/yeah.el), no warnings
  ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
  bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
  pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
  map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
  run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
  gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
  help                  — this text

Exit codes:
  0 — pass       (Green)
  1 — fail       (Red)
  2 — blocked    (input error)
  3 — unknown    (the method could not tell)

Environment:
  MATHC  — path to the math-coding binary (default: `mathc` on PATH)
  EMACS  — path to the Emacs binary (default: `emacs` on PATH)
EOF
    ;;

  smoke)
    echo "yeah-dev ok ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ))"
    exit 0
    ;;

  byte-compile-all)
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    if [ ! -d lib ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: lib/ does not exist" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
    out="$("$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -f batch-byte-compile lib/*.el 2>&1)"
    rc=$?
    clean_bytecode
    printf '%s\n' "$out"
    if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: the compilation failed" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "Warning:"; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: the compilation produced warnings" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    ;;

  ert)
    if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev ert: needs at least one test file" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev ert: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    clean_bytecode
    load_args=()
    for f in "$@"; do
      load_args+=(-l "$f")
    done
    "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -L . "${load_args[@]}" -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
    ;;

  check)
    if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev check: needs at least one check file" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev check: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    clean_bytecode
    rc=0
    started="$(now_ms)"
    for f in "$@"; do
      before="$(now_ms)"
      case "$f" in
        *.el)
          "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -L . -l "$f" || rc=$?
          ;;
        *.sh)
          bash "$f" || rc=$?
          ;;
        *)
          echo "scripts/dev check: unknown kind of check: $f" >&2
          exit 2
          ;;
      esac
      printf 'check: %6d ms  %s\n' "$(( $(now_ms) - before ))" "$f"
    done
    printf 'check: %6d ms  total for %s file(s)\n' "$(( $(now_ms) - started ))" "$#"
    exit $rc
    ;;

  bench)
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev bench: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    if [ ! -f bench/run-bench.el ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev bench: bench/run-bench.el does not exist" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    mode="--self-check"
    for arg in "$@"; do
      case "$arg" in
        --run) mode="--run" ;;
        *)
          echo "scripts/dev bench: unknown option: $arg" >&2
          exit 2
          ;;
      esac
    done
    # The task checks call emacs themselves: EMACS tells them which one.
    # gptel is not part of this repository: YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH names the
    # directory it is installed in, so the Yeah harness can reach a provider.
    clean_bytecode
    gptel_args=()
    if [ -n "${YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH:-}" ]; then
      gptel_args=(-L "$YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH")
    fi
    EMACS="$emacs_bin" "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch "${gptel_args[@]}" -L lib -l bench/run-bench.el -- "$mode"
    exit $?
    ;;

  pixel)
    if [ ! -f tests/pixel/check-interface-is-seen.sh ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev pixel: tests/pixel/check-interface-is-seen.sh does not exist" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    clean_bytecode
    bash tests/pixel/check-interface-is-seen.sh
    exit $?
    ;;

  map)
    need_mathc
    "$mathc_bin" --root . map
    ;;

  run)
    need_mathc
    "$mathc_bin" --root . run
    ;;

  gate)
    need_mathc
    "$mathc_bin" --root . run
    rc=$?
    "$mathc_bin" --root . map
    exit $rc
    ;;

  *)
    echo "scripts/dev: unknown subcommand: $cmd" >&2
    echo "Run \`scripts/dev help\` for the list of subcommands." >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

mathc 5 - source-linked, fresh and independent evidence

Usage: mathc [--root DIR] COMMAND [ARGS]

Start a project:
  mathc adopt
  mathc init
  mathc goal "AIM" "SCOPE[,SCOPE]" "OWNER"
  mathc add ID "TEXT" "SCOPE" "FALSIFIER" fact \
    --requirement "verifier:CMD" --control "BREAK_SUBJECT" [--source ADR]
  mathc run
  mathc map | mathc next | mathc context

Sources and evidence:
  mathc import-adr PATH | mathc import-junit PATH
  mathc re-evaluate
  mathc review-source ID --by OWNER --reason "WHY"

Human decisions (record only what a person actually decided):
  mathc record ID AUTHORITY --by WHO --outcome OUTCOME
  mathc waive ID --by WHO --reason WHY --valid-for DAYS --recovery ACTION
  mathc authorize --by WHO --reason WHY

Other commands:
  mathc install              update only the math-coding block in AGENTS.md
  mathc doctor               check setup without changing it
  mathc mcp                  JSON-RPC over stdio
  mathc help [COMMAND] | mathc --help
  mathc --version

Local binary and agent-skill installation: ./install.sh

Exit codes:
  successful actions and next/context  0
  run/map verdict green                0
  run/map verdict red or protected     1
  usage error                          2
  unknown/vacant/uncomputable          3

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

now_ms() {
  printf '%s' "$(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))"
}

case "$cmd" in
  help|--help|-h)
    cat <<'EOF'
scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper

Subcommands:
  smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
  byte-compile-all      — byte-compile lib/*.el (including lib/yeah.el), no warnings
  ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
  bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
  pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
  map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
  run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
  gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
  help                  — this text

Exit codes:
  0 — pass       (Green)
  1 — fail       (Red)
  2 — blocked    (input error)
  3 — unknown    (the method could not tell)

Environment:
  MATHC  — path to the math-coding binary (default: `mathc` on PATH)
  EMACS  — path to the Emacs binary (default: `emacs` on PATH)
EOF
    ;;

  smoke)
    echo "yeah-dev ok ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ))"
    exit 0
    ;;

  byte-compile-all)
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    if [ ! -d lib ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: lib/ does not exist" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
    out="$("$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -f batch-byte-compile lib/*.el 2>&1)"
    rc=$?
    clean_bytecode
    printf '%s\n' "$out"
    if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: the compilation failed" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "Warning:"; then
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: the compilation produced warnings" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    ;;

  ert)
    if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev ert: needs at least one test file" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev ert: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    clean_bytecode
    load_args=()
    for f in "$@"; do
      load_args+=(-l "$f")
    done
    "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -L . "${load_args[@]}" -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
    ;;

  check)
    if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev check: needs at least one check file" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev check: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    clean_bytecode
    rc=0
    started="$(now_ms)"
    for f in "$@"; do
      before="$(now_ms)"
      case "$f" in
        *.el)
          "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch -L lib -L . -l "$f" || rc=$?
          ;;
        *.sh)
          bash "$f" || rc=$?
          ;;
        *)
          echo "scripts/dev check: unknown kind of check: $f" >&2
          exit 2
          ;;
      esac
      printf 'check: %6d ms  %s\n' "$(( $(now_ms) - before ))" "$f"
    done
    printf 'check: %6d ms  total for %s file(s)\n' "$(( $(now_ms) - started ))" "$#"
    exit $rc
    ;;

  bench)
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev bench: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2
      exit 3
    }
    if [ ! -f bench/run-bench.el ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev bench: bench/run-bench.el does not exist" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    mode="--self-check"
    for arg in "$@"; do
      case "$arg" in
        --run) mode="--run" ;;
        *)
          echo "scripts/dev bench: unknown option: $arg" >&2
          exit 2
          ;;
      esac
    done
    # The task checks call emacs themselves: EMACS tells them which one.
    # gptel is not part of this repository: YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH names the
    # directory it is installed in, so the Yeah harness can reach a provider.
    clean_bytecode
    gptel_args=()
    if [ -n "${YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH:-}" ]; then
      gptel_args=(-L "$YEAH_BENCH_GPTEL_PATH")
    fi
    EMACS="$emacs_bin" "$emacs_bin" -Q --batch "${gptel_args[@]}" -L lib -l bench/run-bench.el -- "$mode"
    exit $?
    ;;

  pixel)
    if [ ! -f tests/pixel/check-interface-is-seen.sh ]; then
      echo "scripts/dev pixel: tests/pixel/check-interface-is-seen.sh does not exist" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    clean_bytecode
    bash tests/pixel/check-interface-is-seen.sh
    exit $?
    ;;

  map)
    need_mathc
    "$mathc_bin" --root . map
    ;;

  run)
    need_mathc
    "$mathc_bin" --root . run
    ;;

  gate)
    need_mathc
    "$mathc_bin" --root . run
    rc=$?
    "$mathc_bin" --root . map
    exit $rc
    ;;

  *)
    echo "scripts/dev: unknown subcommand: $cmd" >&2
    echo "Run \`scripts/dev help\` for the list of subcommands." >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

## The self-development run that found the noise of the provider (2026-11-17, 15:45–15:53)

The next live run was the first run of Yeah on the task of the owner: the wave
41 of the plan (`docs/PLAN.md` §18.1), the deterministic verifier of the
bridge.  The harness ran in a copy of the repository with the code of wave 45
(`/home/az/Projects/yeah-selfdev-1`), the provider was MiniMax-M3 at
`api.minimax.io`, and the model was told that it works in the repository of
Yeah itself.

**The run failed, and the failure was the harness's.**  The journal of the
session (`sessions/wave41.jsonl`, 132 records, 232 577 bytes) holds 17 calls of
tools — `read` eight times, `git_status` three times, `bash` three times, and
`glob`, `grep` and `todo_list` once each — with a permission request and a
permission decision for every one of them, 8 nudges and 9 assistant messages.
The model was working: it read the rules of the repository, searched them, ran
the commands and kept its state.

The provider answered every batch of those results with an empty message.  The
harness read that silence as the silence of a model that does not act, spent
the whole budget of the nudges on it (eight), and ended the run in the state
`failed`.  The last record of the journal said:

Both halves of that sentence were false.  The run had an effect — seventeen

nudges now pays for the nudges that no effect answered: a nudge that follows
the silence of the provider after the tools of the model have come back does
not spend it, and a model that never acts still ends.  The record of a run that
did not finish names the tools the run called, so a run that called its tools
is never described as a run that ended without an effect.

**What the run does not prove.**  The run of wave 41 on the code of wave 46 is
still owed: the fix of wave 46 is checked offline, with a fake transport that
plays the shape of this run, and the shape of a live provider is not the shape
of a fake one.  The run also says nothing about the parity, and nothing about
the working directory of a session: the tools of the run ran in the directory
of the process, and the `cwd` of a session is still not applied to them
(`docs/PLAN.md` §17.1).
